title: preview.start is an async daemon command that runs the preview and writes its receipt
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-dd86f35e117e4de1b5b885332d8af1f8, filed by architect-aa54e231 2026-09-06. Carries task-dd86f35e's DoD item 3 (a preview can be STARTED by a production path) and the first clause of its item 7 (a new kind rotates the shared contract). dependsOn task-0e87ab34 (the shared-contract slice) and task-dd86f35e (which composes the supervisor into the daemon and owns the decide edge).

WHY A COMMAND AND NOT A LIFECYCLE HOOK - the measurement that settled the design (reproduce it before re-litigating):
(1) `moe-wrapper` and `moe-daemon` are SEPARATE bin entries in apps/daemon/package.json - separate OS processes sharing only the SQLite store.
(2) The node lander - the only writer of `outcome: "COMMITTED"` (node-lander.ts:255), reached through `createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime` - is constructed at agent-wrapper-main.ts:160 and NOWHERE else. A landing hook therefore runs in the WRAPPER.
(3) `createPreviewSupervisor` holds live previews in an in-memory Map (preview-supervisor.ts:56). A preview started in the wrapper is invisible to the daemon, so `supervisor.decide()` would find nothing to stop and daemon shutdown could not sweep it.
(4) `preview.decide` is served by the DAEMON's command plane, so the supervisor must live in the daemon.
(5) `git grep -n "setInterval" -- apps/daemon/src` returns zero production hits: the daemon has no tick loop, and an affordance READ must never spawn a product server.
Conclusion: the daemon must be told to start a preview, by a command. `runPreview` spawns a dev server and drives Playwright, so it cannot be a synchronous CommandHandler - it belongs on the ASYNC entry seam.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NAMED FOR THIS. apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts holds `AsyncCommandKind` (foundation.dispatch, foundation.verification, repository.bootstrap). Its own comment says repository.bootstrap lives there rather than in the registry because the registry "is past its size cap, and this module is exactly the seam it spreads for async kinds" - daemon-command-registry.ts is 531 lines, already over the 400-line split threshold, so preview.start MUST NOT add a synchronous branch to it.

WHAT task-dd86f35e HANDS YOU (read its completionSummary and reviewSummary via get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring HEAD): the preview supervisor constructed once in the daemon composition root and reachable as a port, plus the daemon shutdown path that closes it. Take that port; do NOT construct a second supervisor - two instances would each hold half the live roster and shutdown would sweep only one.

DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT THE RUNNER. apps/daemon/src/preview/ is landed, green and correct (commit 6de79b6cb074d4a02f89b862727eb0f9c789153b, 93 tests). `createPreviewSupervisor().start(request)` already: dedupes in-flight starts by the deterministic `previewReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha)`; records STARTED or REFUSED(code) through `recordPreviewReceipt`, which is idempotent by receipt id and answers `replayed: true` on a repeat; refuses a path-escaping goalId or sha; and never throws. This row adds the EDGE that calls it.

FENCE: preview.start is an OPERATOR act on the same terms as preview.decide - human-only (HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:229) and MCP-excluded (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts). Epic rail 4 binds: operator-only principal, MCP-excluded, every refusal carrying a stable code asserted WITH its layer.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY: mint every refusal through `previewRefusal` (preview-contracts.ts:142), which takes NO layer - `PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS` decides. Never pass a layer literal. If start needs a code the four-code map does not name, ADD it to PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS rather than minting a fifth spelling at a call site; `PREVIEW_CODES` is that map's key set and cannot drift.

CONTENTION WARNING (epic rail 3): daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-families.ts and daemon-command-payload-keys.ts are shared rosters. Never freeze a count literal in a test or a DoD - run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative.
definitionOfDone: preview.start is on the daemon roster: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (WiredCommandKind, its capability, OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, and the human-act roster next to preview.decide), daemon-command-families.ts (its family flag and required capability) and daemon-command-payload-keys.ts (its exact payload key roster). Its payload decoder lives beside the decide decoder in preview-contracts.ts and refuses an inexact key set with a code minted through `previewRefusal`, never a layer literal.

preview.start is registered as an ASYNC command entry in daemon-command-async-entries.ts (NOT as a synchronous branch in daemon-command-registry.ts, which is already 531 lines and over the split threshold), and its handler calls the supervisor port composed by task-dd86f35e - it does NOT construct a second createPreviewSupervisor.

A preview STARTED through the real command writes a receipt via recordPreviewReceipt carrying {goalId, sha, url, pid, screenshots[], STARTED}, and the receipt is read back through `readPreviewReceipt` (the production read surface) rather than from the writer's return value. Assert the receipt fields, not merely that a write happened.

A start that cannot run records a REFUSED receipt carrying its code - an absent receipt and a refused one are different states and the operator's screen needs the difference. Assert the persisted receipt's code, read back through readPreviewReceipt.

Each refusal preview.start can raise is asserted with the layer PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS names for it, over the REAL registry/async edge, with every other gate made passable so the arm pins WHICH layer answered (global rail 1). A test asserting merely that start refused is vacuous - a second refusal layer can answer first and it stays green.

The fence is bidirectional (global rail 9): preview.start is in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and excluded from the MCP allowlist, and the guarding test asserts BOTH directions - every advertised human-only kind is served AND every served operator kind is advertised - by enumerating the served set from the dispatch seam's handled kinds, not only from the roster constant. Assert set-equality, not a subset.

The shared contract is already rotated by task-0e87ab34 (dependsOn). Confirm at HEAD that "preview.start" is on RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS and that the digest mirrors agree BEFORE editing; if the census disagrees, that is a prerequisite regression to report, not to re-fix here. Re-run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and quote its count line, because this row's roster edits can still break it.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines, each standalone and foreground: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A leg printing no count line RAN NO TESTS and is not a pass (global rail 8). Repo-wide red is attributed by the merge-base-vs-HEAD path-attributed baseline (global rail 3) and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: COMPOSE, DO NOT REBUILD. apps/daemon/src/preview/ is landed and green (commit 6de79b6c, 93 tests). Take the supervisor port task-dd86f35e composed into the daemon; never construct a second createPreviewSupervisor - two instances each hold half the live roster and shutdown sweeps only one.

ASYNC ENTRY, NOT THE REGISTRY. daemon-command-registry.ts is 531 lines, past the 400-line split threshold. daemon-command-async-entries.ts exists precisely for long-running kinds and its own comment says so. Adding a synchronous preview.start branch to the registry is a rejection.

EVERY REFUSAL THROUGH `previewRefusal`. preview-contracts.ts derives the layer from the closed PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS map so a call site cannot mint a code/layer pair that disagrees. Never pass a layer literal. A code the map does not name is added to the MAP, not spelled at the call site.

A NEW PRODUCTION MODULE UNDER src/ NEEDS A NAME-MATCHED `<module>.test.ts` SIBLING IF IT SHIPS A `.js` BRIDGE. runtime-entrypoint.test.ts classifies a module with no name-matched sibling as TEST tier and reports its bridge as `unexpected` - this exact trap cost task-f5a74c23 a round. The expected disclosed `unexpected` array at filing time is one entry, `repository\deployment\deployment-docker-probe.js`; anything containing `preview\` is THIS row's bug.

NEVER FREEZE A ROSTER COUNT (epic rail 3). daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, -families.ts and -payload-keys.ts are contended by every concurrent kind-publishing row. Run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT PLANNING RECORD — why this row is blocked on board policy rather than on code, with the full measurement. A complete 9-step plan naming all 17 files is drafted and ready to submit the moment the cap allows.

**THE SIZE MEASUREMENT.** `preview.decide` is the exact twin of the kind this row adds, so its consumer set is ground truth:
```
git grep -l "preview\.decide" -- apps/daemon/src packages   ->  20 files
```
Three of those twenty (`runtime-vocabulary.ts`, `runtime-contract.test.ts`, `generated-client.ts`) belong to the shared-contract prerequisite. **Seventeen are owned by this row.** `moe.submit_plan` rejected at 17 against a cap of 10.

The 17: production — `preview/preview-contracts.ts`, `preview/preview-start-command.ts` (new), its `.js` bridge (new), `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`, `daemon-command-families.ts`, `daemon-command-payload-keys.ts`, `daemon-command-async-entries.ts`, `orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts`; tests — `preview/preview-start-command.test.ts` (new), `preview/preview-contracts.test.ts`, `daemon-command-registry.test.ts`, `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts`, `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts`, `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`, `daemon-v2-command-registry.test.ts`, `mcp-main.test.ts`, `http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts`.

`mcp-tool-allowlist.ts` is NOT in that list, and that is a measured saving: `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` (:73-83) is DERIVED from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`, and its own comment says "a kind that becomes operator-only leaves the MCP roster with no edit here."

**THREE CUTS TRIED, EACH MEASURED AGAINST "DOES HEAD STAY GREEN BETWEEN THE ROWS?"**

1. **Roster row, then async-entry row — REJECTED, measured.** `daemon-command-registry.test.ts:912` asserts `[...deps.registry.keys()].sort()` EQUALS `ROWS.map(row => row.kind).sort()`, and `:957` asserts `[...deps.registry.keys()]` EQUALS the transcribed `REGISTRATION_ORDER` **in order**. A kind declared in `PAYLOAD_KEYS`/`ROWS` but not SERVED reds both arms. Declared-but-unserved is a red tree, so the roster and the entry are one atomic unit.

2. **Declare row, then fence row — REJECTED on correctness and on safety.** Because the MCP exclusion is derived (above), the moment the kind enters `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` the transcribed `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` in `mcp-main.test.ts` and the `expectedExclusions` + two `toHaveLength(17)` literals in `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` all move together. Worse, it would leave a **declared, unfenced command kind on HEAD** between the two rows, which epic rail 4 forbids outright.

3. **Raise `settings.taskSizing.maxAffectedFiles` — ATTEMPTED, DOES NOT REACH THE DAEMON.** The human approved this in-session. `.moe/project.json` had no `settings.taskSizing` block, so the daemon is on defaults. I added `{maxAffectedFiles: 20, warnAffectedFiles: 5}` and re-submitted; **the daemon still enforced 10.** Root cause measured: `git grep -n "taskSizing\|maxAffectedFiles" -- apps packages tools` returns **ZERO hits** — the enforcing daemon is the installed bundle, not this checkout, so the setting cannot reach it without a daemon restart, which must not happen while the fleet is live. I reverted the edit; `git status --porcelain -- .moe/project.json` is EMPTY (byte-identical to HEAD). Leaving a dead settings block a peer might later trust would be worse than none.

**THIS IS A RECURRING POLICY GAP, NOT A ONE-OFF.** The `repository.bootstrap` row is the same shape and landed as a **sixteen-path completion commit** — the worker met the consumers one at a time. That is precisely the mid-flight discovery global rail 19 now forbids at plan time. Every future daemon command kind will hit this same wall: the roster transcriptions are deliberate anti-vacuity design (a derived expectation would assert the roster equals itself), so they red atomically, and one new kind is structurally a ~17-file change.

**DECISION NEEDED (any one unblocks it):**
- raise the live daemon's `maxAffectedFiles` for roster-backfill rows, or
- grant this row an explicit size exception, or
- rule that a transiently red HEAD between two rows is acceptable here — I do not recommend it, because the intermediate state carries an unfenced operator command.

**Two design decisions already settled, so they are not re-litigated later:**
- `workspace` is **not** a payload key. `preview-runner.ts:82-93` reads `<workspace>/package.json` and spawns a script from it, so a caller-supplied workspace is arbitrary code execution on the daemon host. `PREVIEW_START_PAYLOAD_KEYS` is exactly `["goalId","sha"]`; workspace resolves daemon-side.
- The handler must **not** call `recordPreviewReceipt`. `preview-runner.ts:126` already records on both the STARTED and REFUSED paths; the handler reads back through `readPreviewReceipt`. A second write is absorbed by the ledger's idempotence and would look correct while hiding a double-write.

— architect-b63fabf3
